_comment: Source of truth for the bookshelf. Add a book by appending an object. cover: filename in assets/books/, or omit to fall back to Open Library by ISBN, then to a typeset card. height: 0.88-1.06, purely visual so the shelf looks like real books. Order here is the order on the shelf.

books.title: Yesteryear
books.author: Caro Claire Burke
books.thought: Such an engaging hook, and unexpectedly funny. I picked it up for the premise and stayed for how sharp it turned out to be underneath the jokes.
books.context: A tradwife influencer wakes up in the brutal reality of 1855. A debut, a #1 New York Times bestseller, and already being adapted with Anne Hathaway attached.

books.title: Yellowface
books.author: R. F. Kuang
books.thought: One of my favourite books of all time. Couldn't put it down, and I love everything about it, right down to how uncomfortable it's willing to make you. The kind of book I've pressed on people who didn't ask.
books.context: A struggling white author steals her dead friend's manuscript and passes it off as her own. Kuang's satire of publishing became one of the most argued-over novels of its year.

books.title: Humankind
books.author: Rutger Bregman
books.thought: A much-needed dose of optimism for a difficult year. It never asks you to be naive about people, which is exactly why the argument lands.
books.context: Bregman's case that people are decent by default, re-examining the evidence behind Lord of the Flies, the Stanford prison experiment and the Blitz.

books.title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
books.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
books.thought: Such beautiful storytelling. It leaves you feeling like you know her, then quietly reminds you that being believed was always the trick she was best at.
books.context: An ageing film star finally tells the truth about her seven marriages, to a journalist who has no idea why she was chosen. A word-of-mouth phenomenon years after it was published.

books.title: Murdoku
books.author: Manuel Garand
books.thought: Super fun and super addictive. You just have to try it to know it.
books.context: Eighty murder-mystery logic puzzles: sudoku grids turned into crime scenes, where you place the suspects to reveal the killer. A USA Today and Publishers Weekly bestseller, by a puzzle maker whose work has run in the Financial Times.
